Question: Can agents operate at configurable autonomy tiers (fully supervised to fully autonomous)? Does autonomy adjust based on task risk, confidence score, and historical success rate?
Response: Yes. Autonomy is governed by configurable thresholds stored in the workflow configuration store and adjustable at runtime via the Control Plane without redeployment. The agentic loop reads thresholds at phase start and makes autonomy decisions accordingly. Example (POC2 screening): confidence >85% -> auto-shortlist (fully autonomous), 60-85% -> route to HR BP exception queue (supervised), <60% -> auto-reject (autonomous low-risk decision). Thresholds adjust based on: (1) Task risk — high-value invoices or senior hires require lower autonomy thresholds. (2) Confidence score — the model's stated confidence on the decision. (3) Historical success rate — the Fleet Manager analyses override patterns and proposes threshold adjustments when operators consistently override at certain confidence levels. Threshold changes are audit-logged with operator identity, timestamp, and rationale. GHCP SDK hooks enforce the thresholds — actions that would exceed autonomy boundaries are intercepted and routed to the human's PA.
Key Technologies: Configurable thresholds (runtime-adjustable), GHCP SDK hooks (enforcement), Fleet Manager (threshold proposals), Control Plane UI (autonomy dials)
POC Demo: POC2: Show autonomy dials on Control Plane — adjust screening auto-shortlist threshold from 85% to 75%, show immediate effect on next screening phase. Show audit trail of the change.

Question: Describe the formal process for moving workflows from experimental (generative) to standardised (deterministic): observation, statistical validation, code generation, review, promotion, monitoring.
Response: The crystallisation pipeline follows a formal progression. (1) Observation: agentic loops execute generatively — the LLM reasons through tasks, and all execution is traced via OTEL. (2) Statistical validation: after N successful executions (configurable), the Fleet Manager analyses outcome consistency and quality scores from Foundry Evaluators. (3) Code generation: consistent patterns are extracted into deterministic code by the agentic builder or a developer. (4) Review: human reviews the deterministic implementation via Control Plane or PR. (5) Promotion: the crystallised skill is registered in Azure API Center, promoted through Design -> Preview -> Production with approval gates at each stage. (6) Monitoring: the crystallised skill runs deterministically in production. Foundry Evaluators monitor quality against the generative baseline. If quality degrades, the Fleet Manager alerts the operator. Exception fallback: if the crystallised skill encounters a novel exception, it falls back to generative orchestration, logs the exception, and the exception feeds into the next crystallisation cycle.
Key Technologies: Skill crystallisation pipeline, Azure API Center lifecycle, Foundry Evaluators, Fleet Manager monitoring, OTEL observation

Question: Can crystallised workflows invoke generative orchestration when encountering novel exceptions? Are exceptions logged, analysed, and fed into new crystallisation cycles?
Response: Yes. Crystallised skills include exception handling: when a deterministic skill encounters input it cannot process (novel CV format, unexpected invoice structure), it raises an exception rather than failing silently. The Durable Functions orchestration catches the exception and triggers a new agentic loop with the full generative capability — the LLM reasons about the novel situation with all available context. The exception is: (1) Logged with full context (what the crystallised skill tried, why it failed, what the input was). (2) Analysed by the Fleet Manager — is this a one-off anomaly or a pattern? (3) Fed into the next crystallisation cycle — if similar exceptions recur, the deterministic skill is updated to handle the new pattern. The entire cycle is visible on the Control Plane: operators see which skills are crystallised, their exception rates, and pending crystallisation proposals.
Key Technologies: Crystallised skills (exception handling), Durable Functions (fallback orchestration), Fleet Manager (pattern analysis), Control Plane (visibility)
POC Demo: POC2: Show crystallised CV parser encountering novel format — fallback to generative, successful processing, exception logged for next crystallisation cycle.

Question: Describe policy-as-code enforcement across the full agent lifecycle. Are policies: version-controlled, adaptive (runtime context), composable (inheritance), audit-trailed, and testable (dry-run against historical traces)?
Response: Governance-as-code operates across multiple layers, all Git-committed and version-controlled. (1) Version-controlled: APIM policies via APIOps CI/CD, GHCP SDK hooks in Git, Foundry Guardrails configuration per agent, jurisdiction-specific skills as SKILL.md files, autonomy thresholds in config store with change tracking. (2) Adaptive: policies adapt to runtime context — jurisdiction-specific skills load based on workflow context, APIM routes based on jurisdiction metadata, autonomy thresholds are per-workflow adjustable. (3) Composable: skills inherit base governance from their domain (all hiring skills inherit GDPR rules), and layer jurisdiction-specific rules on top (German hires add works council notifications). APIM policies compose with inheritance. (4) Audit-trailed: every policy change is logged with author, timestamp, rationale. Every enforcement decision is logged via OTEL and APIM. (5) Testable: policies can be evaluated against historical traces via Foundry Evaluators — 'if we change this threshold, how many past cases would have been affected?' This enables policy dry-run before deployment.
Key Technologies: APIOps CI/CD, GHCP SDK hooks, Foundry Guardrails, jurisdiction skills, Foundry Evaluators (dry-run), OTEL audit
